name: AGC 215286 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 215286, an irregular galaxy in the Local Volume, seen by Hubble.
label: agc215286-hubble
story: An amorphous, irregular galaxy among our nearer neighbors. Hubble resolved its stars to measure its distance, helping test whether the lowest-mass galaxies rotate faster than the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation predicts.

claims.text: AGC 215286 is a galaxy classed as amorphous irregular, targeted by Hubble program 17480
The program's targets are Local Volume galaxies
Hubble measures their distances from the red giant branch tip using resolved stars
Low mass galaxies are predicted to have higher Vmax than the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation extrapolated from higher masses
